cands.name: Gloria Romero Roses
cands.bio: Democrat, businesswoman. Principal of NEXUS Living LLC since 2008; owns an assisted living facility; former Continental Group communications director and Climate First Bank shareholder/adviser. MBA, University of Miami. First run for office per sources found.
cands.local_ties: Born in Bogota, Colombia, raised in South Florida, per her campaign site; residence not stated.

record.text: Board service listed on campaign site: Univision Foundation, genCLEO Action, Women's Fund of Miami-Dade; Alzheimer's Association advocate. No prior elected office found.
Priorities per campaign: faster affordable-housing construction, insurance accountability and hurricane hardening, childcare, an 'Elder's Trust' for senior programs.

endorsements.text: Latino Victory Fund (progressive PAC) endorsed her in March 2026.

cands.gaps: Photo not verified (none retrieved). Donors and committee support not found. Owner-source search NOT run (shared web-search budget exhausted).

cands.name: Bruno Barreiro
cands.bio: Republican, businessman. Florida House District 107, 1992-1998; Miami-Dade County Commissioner, District 5, 1998-2018. Owner of BABJ Investment Corp.; director at IUSA Water and Fatima Home Care. Lost 2018 U.S. House primary and 2020 HD 112 race.
cands.local_ties: Born in Clearwater to Cuban immigrant parents; campaign says he grew up, opened his business and raised his family in Miami. Campaign HQ 1454 SW 1 St, Miami. Home address not stated.

record.text: Miami-Dade Commission chair in 2007-2008 per Wikipedia (his campaign site says 2006); key figure behind Marlins Park. Lost 2018 GOP primary for FL-27 to Maria Elvira Salazar (40.5% to 25.7%) and the 2020 HD 112 general to Nick Duran (53% to 47%).

Campaign site claims he created the Golden Passport for Seniors, sponsored the first senior tax exemption expansion in the Legislature, and supports condo reform and cutting taxes and fees (campaign claims).

money_notes.text: Wikipedia reports that in 2018 he used over $95,000 of his own campaign funds to support his wife Zoraida's special-election bid for his former seat; she lost to Eileen Higgins.

controversies.text: In 2012 Barreiro, then a Miami-Dade commissioner, voted to award a $25 million Metrorail test-track contract to Munilla Construction. The Miami New Times, citing the Miami Herald, reported that four Munilla family members had given him maximum donations. It also reported that he rented office space from the family and called them close friends. The track was two years late by August 2016.

cands.gaps: Endorsements not named on his site; 2026 donors not found. Controversy items come from Wikipedia only (secondhand). Primary win over Frank Lago and Tony Diaz was reported only through a search summary of county results; exact margin not confirmed. Owner-source search NOT run (shared web-search budget exhausted).
